what: 🌿 FRESH — Forage Resource Evaluation System for Habitat
title: Utilities and Data Visualization Tools for Ecology
text: fresh() computes maximum suitable forage biomass meets minimum digestible energy (DE) digestible protein (DP) concentration constraints generalist herbivore, using linear programming. One LP solved per patch_id. returns fresh_output object $summary (one row per patch x constraint pair), $detail table (per-forage contributions), , habitat_type column supplied, $habitat summary.
code: library(ecologytools)  #--------------------------------------- # 1. Minimal single-constraint example #--------------------------------------- # Forage biomass: one row per forage per patch (grams over a sampled area) biomass_data <- data.frame(   patch_id = c("A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "B"),   plant_id = c("Vaccinium", "Carex", "Salix", "Vaccinium", "Carex", "Salix"),   biomass = c(120, 80, 45, 60, 150, 30),   area = 900 )  # Nutritional values: one row per plant_id nutrition_data <- data.frame(   plant_id = c("Vaccinium", "Carex", "Salix"),   de = c(12.5, 9.8, 11.2), # kJ/g   dp = c(9.0, 5.5, 8.1), # g / 100 g   diet_proportion = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2) )  result <- fresh(   biomass_data = biomass_data,   nutrition_data = nutrition_data,   animal_de_req = 11.5, # minimum diet DE (kJ/g)   animal_dp_req = 7.5, # minimum diet DP (g / 100 g)   animal_dmi = 1500 # daily dry matter intake (g/day) )  result # S3 print method: quick FRESH summary result$summary # suitable biomass, animal-days, limiting constraint, etc. result$detail # biomass used and proportions per forage  #--------------------------------------- # 2. Multiple constraint pairs at once #--------------------------------------- # Passing vectors solves each (de_req, dp_req) pair as a separate scenario. multi <- fresh(   biomass_data = biomass_data,   nutrition_data = nutrition_data,   animal_de_req = c(10.5, 11.5, 12.5),   animal_dp_req = c(6.0, 7.5, 9.0) ) multi$summary

title: Utilities and Data Visualization Tools for Ecology
code: library(ggplot2) library(ecologytools)  #--------------------------------------- # 1. Scatter plot with many colors #--------------------------------------- set.seed(1) df_point <- data.frame(   x = rnorm(200),   y = rnorm(200),   group = sample(letters[1:7], 200, replace = TRUE) ) ggplot(df_point, aes(x, y, color = group)) +   geom_point(size = 2) +   scale_color_martin("discrete") +   theme_martin()  #--------------------------------------- # 2. Line plot with a continuous gradient #--------------------------------------- df_line <- data.frame(   x = rep(1:50, 6),   y = c(     cumsum(rnorm(50)),     cumsum(rnorm(50)),     cumsum(rnorm(50)),     cumsum(rnorm(50)),     cumsum(rnorm(50)),     cumsum(rnorm(50))   ),   group = rep(1:6, each = 50) ) ggplot(df_line, aes(x, y, color = group, group = group)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   scale_color_martin("earth") +   theme_martin()  #--------------------------------------- # 3. Facet wrap example #--------------------------------------- df_facet <- data.frame(   x = rep(1:20, 4),   y = rnorm(80),   group = rep(letters[1:4], each = 20) ) ggplot(df_facet, aes(x, y)) +   geom_line(color = pal("black"), linewidth = 1) +   facet_wrap(~group) +   theme_martin()  #--------------------------------------- # 4. Plant functional groups #--------------------------------------- df_plants <- data.frame(   group = factor(     c("grass", "shrub", "forb", "tree", "fern"),     levels = c("grass", "shrub", "forb", "tree", "fern")   ),   cover = c(45, 22, 18, 10, 5) ) ggplot(df_plants, aes(x = group, y = cover, fill = group)) +   geom_col() +   scale_fill_martin("plants") +   theme_martin() +   theme(legend.position = "none")  #--------------------------------------- # 5. Plant phenology #--------------------------------------- df_phen <- data.frame(   stage = factor(     rep(c("emergent", "flower", "fruiting", "mature", "senesced"), each = 20),     levels = c("emergent", "flower", "fruiting", "mature", "senesced")   ),   biomass = c(     rnorm(20, 5, 1),     rnorm(20, 12, 2),     rnorm(20, 15, 2),     rnorm(20, 10, 2),     rnorm(20, 3, 1)   ) ) ggplot(df_phen, aes(x = stage, y = biomass, fill = stage)) +   geom_boxplot() +   scale_fill_martin("phenology") +   theme_martin() +   theme(legend.position = "none")  #--------------------------------------- # 6. Season #--------------------------------------- df_season <- data.frame(   doy = rep(1:90, 4),   ndvi = c(     rnorm(90, 0.3, 0.05),     rnorm(90, 0.7, 0.05),     rnorm(90, 0.5, 0.05),     rnorm(90, 0.2, 0.05)   ),   season = factor(     rep(c("spring", "summer", "fall", "winter"), each = 90),     levels = c("spring", "summer", "fall", "winter")   ) ) ggplot(df_season, aes(x = doy, y = ndvi, color = season)) +   geom_point() +   scale_color_martin("season") +   theme_martin()  #--------------------------------------- # 7. Gender #--------------------------------------- df_gender <- data.frame(   mass = c(rnorm(40, 75, 8), rnorm(40, 60, 7), rnorm(10, 65, 10)),   sex = factor(     c(rep("male", 40), rep("female", 40), rep("unknown", 10)),     levels = c("male", "female", "unknown")   ) ) ggplot(df_gender, aes(x = sex, y = mass, fill = sex)) +   geom_violin() +   scale_fill_martin("gender") +   theme_martin() +   theme(legend.position = "none")  #--------------------------------------- # 8. Temperature gradient #--------------------------------------- df_temp <- expand.grid(x = 1:20, y = 1:20) df_temp$temp <- with(df_temp, sin(x / 3) + cos(y / 3) + rnorm(nrow(df_temp), 0, 0.2)) ggplot(df_temp, aes(x, y, fill = temp)) +   geom_tile() +   scale_fill_martin("temp") +   theme_martin() library(ecologytools)  pal("discrete") # full discrete palette (hex vector) pal("discrete", n = 3) # first 3 discrete colors pal("plants") # named functional-group colors pal("base") # list of white / black / grid utility colors pal("temp") # a continuous gradient's stops  pal_continuous_n(256) # 256 colors interpolated from the "cont" gradient

code: library(terra) library(ecologytools) # Create a smooth synthetic elevation surface r <- rast(nrows = 100, ncols = 100, xmin = 0, xmax = 100, ymin = 0, ymax = 100) xy <- as.data.frame(crds(r)) z <- with(xy,   800 +     250 * exp(-((x - 30)^2 + (y - 35)^2) / 250) +     180 * exp(-((x - 70)^2 + (y - 65)^2) / 180) -     120 * exp(-((x - 55)^2 + (y - 45)^2) / 120) +     60 * sin(x / 8) * cos(y / 10) ) values(r) <- z d <- dist_escape(r, escape_slope = 65) plot(d, main = "Distance to escape terrain") library(ecologytools) library(terra) # create example DEM r <- rast(nrows = 100, ncols = 100, xmin = 0, xmax = 100, ymin = 0, ymax = 100) xy <- as.data.frame(crds(r)) z <- with(   xy,   800 +     250 * exp(-((x - 30)^2 + (y - 35)^2) / 250) +     180 * exp(-((x - 70)^2 + (y - 65)^2) / 180) -     120 * exp(-((x - 55)^2 + (y - 45)^2) / 120) ) values(r) <- z # compute local ruggedness rug <- vrml(r, s = 5) # plot plot(rug, main = "Vector Ruggedness of Local Relief") library(ecologytools) library(terra) # create example time-series raster (5 layers) r <- rast(nrows = 50, ncols = 50, nlyrs = 5) values(r) <- runif(ncell(r) * nlyr(r)) # compute time since peak IRG out <- days_since_peak_IRG(r) # absolute distance from peak (optional) out_abs <- days_since_peak_IRG(r, absolute_value = TRUE) # plot one layer plot(out, main = "Days Since Peak IRG") library(ecologytools) library(terra) # create example raster with 12 layers (e.g., daily data) r <- rast(nrows = 50, ncols = 50, nlyrs = 12) values(r) <- runif(ncell(r) * nlyr(r)) # aggregate into 3-layer periods (e.g., 3-day means) out <- aggregate_raster(r, n = 3, fun = mean) # plot first aggregated layer plot(out, main = "Aggregated Raster") library(ecologytools) library(terra) # a raster that may reference an on-disk source r <- rast(nrows = 50, ncols = 50, vals = runif(2500)) # read all values into memory so the object is safe to serialize r <- force_inmemory(r) inMemory(r) # now safe to wrap + save (e.g., for a compute cluster) # saveRDS(wrap(r), "raster.rds") library(ecologytools) library(terra) r <- rast(nrows = 10, ncols = 10, vals = runif(100)) # prints a formatted diagnostic summary (class, layers, extent, CRS, range, ...) raster_summary(r, name = "example_raster")  # also accepts a PackedSpatRaster; it is unwrapped automatically raster_summary(wrap(r), name = "packed_raster") library(ecologytools) set.seed(1) # synthetic GPS data: two individuals, projected coordinates, POSIXct times gps_df <- data.frame(   x = c(rnorm(30, 500000, 50), rnorm(30, 500500, 50)),   y = c(rnorm(30, 4800000, 50), rnorm(30, 4800400, 50)),   ID = rep(c("ewe_01", "ewe_02"), each = 30),   DateTime = Sys.time() - runif(60, 0, 6 * 86400) )  # DBSCAN-clustered convex-hull search areas from recent locations. # NOTE: also writes last_locations.kml, movement_paths.kml, and # search_areas.kml to the current working directory. areas <- sheep_cluster(   GPS = gps_df,   no.days = 7,   minimum.points = 10,   epsilon = 100,   crs = "EPSG:32612",   filetype = "KML",   basic.plot = TRUE ) areas

title: Utilities and Data Visualization Tools for Ecology
text: calc_diet_quality() ties diet pipeline together: weights taxon’s stage-specific forage quality RRA produce per-sample DP DE. consumes phenology table calc_phenology_mode() (mode), stage-keyed quality table (qual, keyed level name plus Phenology Part), taxonomy crosswalk (lookup).
code: library(ecologytools) set.seed(1) dat <- data.frame(   Date = as.POSIXct("2022-07-01", tz = "UTC") +     sample(0:430, 200, replace = TRUE) * 86400,   Phenology = sample(c("N/B", "FL", "FR", "M", NA), 200, replace = TRUE),   Species = sample(c("Vaccinium membranaceum", "Chimaphila umbellata"), 200, replace = TRUE),   Genus = sample(c("Vaccinium", "Chimaphila"), 200, replace = TRUE),   Family = sample(c("Ericaceae", "Rosaceae"), 200, replace = TRUE),   Functional.Group = sample(c("EVERGREEN SHRUB", "DECIDUOUS SHRUB"), 200, replace = TRUE),   Growth.Form = "SHRUB",   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) # modal phenology code per 14-day period, for each grouping level res <- calc_phenology_mode(dat, length = 14) res$Genus res$All library(ecologytools) forage <- data.frame(   Code = c("VACMEM", "VACMEM", "CARGEY", "CARGEY"),   Scientific.Name = c("Vaccinium membranaceum", "Vaccinium membranaceum",                        "Carex geyeri", "Carex geyeri"),   Genus = c("Vaccinium", "Vaccinium", "Carex", "Carex"),   Family = c("Ericaceae", "Ericaceae", "Cyperaceae", "Cyperaceae"),   Functional.Group = c("DECIDUOUS SHRUB", "DECIDUOUS SHRUB", "GRAMINOID", "GRAMINOID"),   Growth.Form = c("SHRUB", "SHRUB", "GRAMINOID", "GRAMINOID"),   DE = c(12.1, 11.8, 9.5, 9.9), # digestible energy   DP = c(8.8, 9.2, 5.4, 5.8), # digestible protein   DMD = c(0.62, 0.60, 0.55, 0.57) # dry matter digestibility ) # mean, sd, and non-NA n for DE/DP/DMD at each available level summaries <- plant_quality_summary(forage) summaries$species summaries$genus library(ecologytools) # sample-by-taxon relative read abundance (RRA); rows already normalized rra <- data.frame(   "Vaccinium membranaceum" = c(0.5, 0.2),   "Carex geyeri" = c(0.3, 0.5),   "Pinaceae" = c(0.2, 0.3),   check.names = FALSE ) lookup <- data.frame(   Scientific.Name = c("Vaccinium membranaceum", "Carex geyeri"),   Genus = c("Vaccinium", "Carex"),   Family = c("Ericaceae", "Cyperaceae"),   Order = c("Ericales", "Poales") ) props <- calc_diet_prop(rra, lookup) props$species props$genus library(ecologytools)  # `mode` comes from calc_phenology_mode() (one modal-code column per period) mode <- calc_phenology_mode(dat, length = 14)  # `qual` is a list of stage-specific quality tibbles by level, e.g. #   qual$species, qual$genus, ... each with columns: #   <level name>, Phenology, Part, DP_mean, DE_mean # `lookup` is a crosswalk with lowercase columns: #   species, genus, family, order, functional_group, growth_form # `rra` has the meta columns in `meta_cols` plus one numeric column per taxon, #   each row summing to 1.  out <- calc_diet_quality(   rra = rra,   qual = qual,   mode = mode,   lookup = lookup,   meta_cols = c("sample_id", "animal_id", "date", "year", "UTME", "UTMN") ) out$quality # per-sample DP, DE, and coverage out$dropped # audit of taxa excluded from each sample, with reasons

what: Summarize diet proportions from RRA metabarcoding data — calc_diet_prop
title: Summarize diet proportions from RRA metabarcoding data — calc_diet_prop
text: Computes per-taxon diet proportion summaries species, genus, family, order resolutions sample--taxon relative read abundance (RRA) matrix. Within sample, RRA values summed taxonomic group; resulting per-sample proportions summarized across samples max + sd, capped 1, returned diet_proportion.

title: Summarize diet proportions from RRA metabarcoding data — calc_diet_prop
code: calc_diet_prop(rra, lookup, resolve = c("all", "skip"))

title: Summarize diet proportions from RRA metabarcoding data — calc_diet_prop
text: rra data frame, tibble, numeric matrix samples rows taxa columns. Column names taxon identifiers (e.g., "Abies lasiocarpa", "Pinaceae"). columns must numeric, row assumed already normalized (e.g., sum 1). lookup taxonomy table containing minimum columns Scientific.Name, Genus, Family, Order. columns missing, warning issued affected rank skipped (returned NULL output list). resolve Either "" (default) "skip". "", columns resolved rank appear every level's output diet_proportion = NA_real_. "skip", unresolved columns silently dropped.

title: Summarize diet proportions from RRA metabarcoding data — calc_diet_prop
text: named list elements species, genus, family, order. species element two columns (species, diet_proportion). genus, family, order elements include additional logical column (genus_in_lookup, family_in_lookup, order_in_lookup) indicating whether rolled-taxon name found lookup. level whose required lookup column absent returned NULL.

title: Summarize diet proportions from RRA metabarcoding data — calc_diet_prop
text: input column assigned rank follows: Species: exact match lookup$Scientific.Name. Genus: two-word column name parsed first whitespace- separated token treated genus; single-word column name used . cases, resulting genus contributes genus, family, order outputs. genus_in_lookup flag indicates whether genus appears lookup$Genus. Family: single-word columns match genus level checked lookup$Family. Order: single-word columns match genus family level checked lookup$Order. Higher-rank rollups two-word columns obtained looking first-token genus deduplicated Genus → Family/Order table (first occurrence retained). Genus-rank columns roll way; family-rank columns roll order via lookup$Family → lookup$Order (first occurrence retained). Two-word columns whose first token lookup$Genus receive NA family/order rollups contribute genus level (genus_in_lookup = FALSE).

what: Weighted Diet Quality of RRA Samples — calc_diet_quality
title: Weighted Diet Quality of RRA Samples — calc_diet_quality
text: Computes per-sample digestible protein (DP) digestible energy (DE) relative-read-abundance (RRA) diet metabarcoding samples, weighting taxon's stage-specific forage quality RRA. sample, every taxon resolved taxonomic level via lookup, assigned phenological stage mode sample's seasonal period, given DP/DE value qual stage. sample score RRA-weighted mean taxa yield usable value, computed independently DP DE.

title: Weighted Diet Quality of RRA Samples — calc_diet_quality
code: calc_diet_quality(   rra,   qual,   mode,   lookup,   meta_cols = c("sample_id", "animal_id", "date", "year", "UTME", "UTMN"),   tol = 1e-06 )

title: Weighted Diet Quality of RRA Samples — calc_diet_quality
text: rra data frame RRA samples: columns named meta_cols plus one numeric column per taxon, row summing 1. qual list quality tibbles level (species, genus, family, functional_group, growth_form), keyed level's name column plus Phenology Part, DP_mean DE_mean. mode list phenology summaries level (five plus ), returned calc_phenology_mode: key column one modal-code column per seasonal period. lookup taxonomy crosswalk columns species, genus, family, order, functional_group, growth_form. meta_cols Character vector non-taxon columns rra. Defaults c('sample_id', 'animal_id', 'date', 'year', 'UTME', 'UTMN'). tol Numeric tolerance per-row sum--1 check. Defaults 1e-6.

title: Weighted Diet Quality of RRA Samples — calc_diet_quality
text: list two data frames. quality one row per sample: meta_cols, DP, DE, dp_coverage / de_coverage (summed RRA actually scored metric). dropped one row per dropped taxon-sample: sample_id, rra_taxon, rra_value, entry_level, reason (unresolved, moss, na_phenology, na_quality_DP, na_quality_DE).

title: Weighted Diet Quality of RRA Samples — calc_diet_quality
text: Resolution fall-: taxon column name matched lookup species (binomial), genus (first word binomial, single-word name), family, order; functional_group growth_form taken modal value across matched rows. Phenology assigned precedence order: MOSS either group field drops taxon, TREE forces T, FERN forces FE, otherwise mode searched taxon's level first non-NA code period. Quality read Part == '' starting taxon's resolved level walking coarser levels whenever row missing value NA. Taxa found lookup, dropped MOSS, lacking phenology code, lacking usable quality value excluded weight removed; surviving weights form metric's denominator.

what: Modal Phenology by Period Across Grouping Levels — calc_phenology_mode
title: Modal Phenology by Period Across Grouping Levels — calc_phenology_mode
text: Bins vegetation observations fixed-width calendar periods anchored month-day starting_date (default July 1) computes modal Phenology code within period several grouping levels. Periods defined number days since recent anchor date observation, seasonal window pooled across years present data (e.g., 'Jul 01-Jul 14' cell combines window every year).

title: Modal Phenology by Period Across Grouping Levels — calc_phenology_mode
code: calc_phenology_mode(   dat,   starting_date = as.POSIXct(x = "2000-07-01", tz = "UTC"),   length = 14 )

title: Modal Phenology by Period Across Grouping Levels — calc_phenology_mode
text: dat data frame (tibble) containing least columns Date (POSIXct column), Phenology, Species, Genus, Family, Functional.Group, Growth.Form. starting_date length-one POSIXct giving seasonal anchor. month day used; year ignored anchor generalizes every year dat. Defaults July 1. length Integer. Width period calendar days. Defaults 14.

title: Modal Phenology by Period Across Grouping Levels — calc_phenology_mode
text: named list six data frames. first five (Species, Genus, Family, Functional.Group, Growth.Form) one row per level grouping column one column per period; sixth () single row summarizing observations. Period columns labelled date range (e.g., 'Jul 01-Jul 14') ordered anchor last period containing observations, gaps. Cells contain modal phenology code, NA fewer three observations exist.

title: Modal Phenology by Period Across Grouping Levels — calc_phenology_mode
text: Within group-period, mode frequent phenology code, computed least three non-missing observations present (otherwise cell NA). Ties broken earliest phenological stage fixed order N/B < FL < FR < M < C < T < FE. NA phenology values ignored counting computing mode; trigger error. non-NA value outside seven allowed codes causes error computation done.

title: Forage Resource Evaluation System for Habitat (FRESH) — fresh
text: biomass_data Long-format data frame one row per forage per patch. Required columns: plant_id (character), biomass (numeric). Optional columns: patch_id (character factor) – groups rows patches; one LP solved per patch. absent, rows treated single patch warning issued. plant_part plant_phenology (character) – subdivides species parts different nutritional values (e.g., leaves vs. twigs). Must match column name used nutrition_data. absent tables, join uses plant_id . area (numeric, m^2) – area biomass collected. Must constant within patch. Overridden area argument supplied. habitat_type (integer, factor, character) – habitat classification row. present, $habitat element added output per-habitat-type summaries averaged across patches. Also propagated $detail output column. nutrition_data Lookup data frame, one row per plant_id (part). Required columns: plant_id (character), de (numeric), dp (numeric), diet_proportion (numeric, 0–1). Optional columns: plant_part plant_phenology (character) – must match column name used biomass_data. sd_de sd_dp (numeric) – standard deviations de dp. must present neither. present, forage expanded low/mid/high SD groups LP (proportions 0.16 / 0.68 / 0.16 normal distribution), allowing partial inclusion forages near nutritional threshold. Forages NA SD values stay single (mean) group. biomass_unit Unit biomass column. "g" (default) "kg". de_unit Unit de column animal_de_req. "kj_g" (default) "kcal_g". dmi_unit Unit animal_dmi. "g_day" (default) "kg_day". output_area_unit Unit output biomass densities animal days. One "kg_ha" (default), "g_m2", "g_900m2", "kg_m2", "g_ha". area Scalar area m^2 biomass collected. supplied biomass_data area column, argument wins (warning). least one two must present. animal_de_req Minimum digestible energy concentration diet, units matching de_unit. Scalar numeric vector. Default 11.5 (kJ/g, corresponding moderate-quality diet roughly 60% dry matter digestibility generalist herbivore). animal_de_req animal_dp_req vectors must length, pair (animal_de_req[], animal_dp_req[]) separate LP solve per patch, producing separate row summary separate set rows detail. one scalar vector, scalar recycled match vector's length. animal_dp_req Minimum digestible protein concentration diet, g/100g dry matter. Scalar numeric vector; recycling vector behavior described animal_de_req. Default 7.5 (intermediate value body-maintenance lactation requirements medium-sized cervid). animal_dmi Daily dry matter intake, units matching dmi_unit. Optional; NULL, animal_days_per_area output NA. max_any_forage_prop Scalar [0, 1]. Caps proportion single forage (summed across SD groups) diet. Intended enforce dietary diversity generalist herbivores tolerate single forage dominating diet. Default 1 (effect). min_total_biomass Scalar >= 0, output_area_unit. Subtracted total suitable biomass computing animal days. Acts foraging efficiency floor: biomass density, herbivores forage profitably regardless forage quality. Default 0 (effect). warnings Logical. TRUE (default), warnings issued call printed console usual. FALSE, suppressed console. Either way, warning messages collected returned warnings element output object.

title: Forage Resource Evaluation System for Habitat (FRESH) — fresh
text: object class "fresh_output": list following components. summary – tibble one row per patch x constraint pair. Columns: patch_id, de_req, dp_req, total_biomass_available, suitable_biomass, pct_suitable_biomass, animal_days_per_area, mean_de_total, mean_dp_total, mean_de_suitable, mean_dp_suitable, n_forages_used, limiting_constraint. logical infeasible column added least one row infeasible. detail – tibble one row per forage per patch per constraint pair (SD groups collapsed back biological forage). Columns: patch_id, de_req, dp_req, plant_id, plant_part plant_phenology (present input), habitat_type (present input), biomass_available, biomass_used, prop_used, prop_of_total. habitat – tibble one row per habitat type x constraint pair, present biomass_data contains habitat_type column. Columns: habitat_type, de_req, dp_req, mean_total_biomass_per_area, mean_suitable_biomass_per_area, mean_de_total, mean_dp_total, mean_de_suitable, mean_dp_suitable. Means simple averages across patches habitat type occurs; patches absent excluded denominator. call – matched call. inputs – named list resolved argument values (units, area, constraints, internal flags indicating whether nutritional variation habitat summaries active). data – list biomass_data nutrition_data supplied user. warnings – character vector warning messages issued call, string "warnings" none fired.

title: Forage Resource Evaluation System for Habitat (FRESH) — fresh
text: implementation follows linear-programming formulation Hanley et al. (2012) departs original following ways: summer--winter conversion. function season-agnostic; users pre-convert biomass nutritional values winter analysis. snow submodel. original derives snow depth elevation, slope, aspect, canopy cover; implemented. landscape/GIS application. stand-level analysis supported. patch_id solved independently. Nutritional variation uses normal-distribution probability mass low/mid/high SD groups (0.16 / 0.68 / 0.16) rather equal thirds (1/3 / 1/3 / 1/3) used Hanley et al. probability-based discretization statistically consistent assumption normality implied reporting SDs first place. Infeasible LP solves return NA rather 0, infeasible column added summary. min_total_biomass specified user's chosen output_area_unit rather fixed kg/ha.

title: Forage Resource Evaluation System for Habitat (FRESH) — fresh
text: Hanley, T..; Spalinger, D.E.; Mock, K.J.; Weaver, O.L.; Harris, G.M. 2012. Forage resource evaluation system habitat–deer: interactive deer habitat model. Gen. Tech. Rep. PNW-GTR-858. Portland, : U.S. Department Agriculture, Forest Service, Pacific Northwest Research Station. 64 p. https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/40300

title: Vector ruggedness of local relief (VRML) — vrml
text: standard vector ruggedness measure (VRM; Sappington et al. 2007) quantifies terrain ruggedness three-dimensional dispersion vectors orthogonal terrain surface, integrating variation slope aspect. produces dimensionless measure surface heterogeneity less correlated slope traditional ruggedness indices. vrml() function modifies approach first smoothing DEM using focal mean filter subtracting original DEM. isolates fine-scale (local) topographic variation removing broad-scale elevation trends. Vector ruggedness computed residual surface using vrm(). result: vrm() measures total terrain heterogeneity across scales present DEM. vrml() emphasizes local relief removing low-frequency structure (e.g., large slopes elevational gradients) prior calculating ruggedness. distinction important VRM captures variation slope aspect independent overall gradient, allowing ruggedness slope treated separate ecological predictors. applying VRM detrended surface, vrml() isolates microtopographic complexity may relevant processes operating finer spatial scales (e.g., movement constraints, microhabitat selection).

title: Vector ruggedness of local relief (VRML) — vrml

title: Vector ruggedness of local relief (VRML) — vrml
